sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Barbell Bicep Curl is an isolation exercise that primarily targets the biceps brachii.

It is one of the most effective exercises for building bicep size and strength, using a barbell to allow you to load heavier weights than dumbbell variations.

This movement is a staple in any arm training program and is suitable for all experience levels.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Builds bicep size and peak
- Increases arm strength for pulling movements
- Allows heavier loading compared to dumbbell curls
- Improves grip and forearm strength
- Enhances muscle definition in the upper arms
- Simple movement pattern, easy to learn
- Carries over to compound pulling exercises like rows and pull-ups

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Biceps Brachii

Secondary: Brachialis, Brachioradialis, Forearms

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Stand straight holding a barbell with an underhand (supinated) grip.
2. Hands should be shoulder-width apart.
3. Arms fully extended towards the floor.
4. Keep your elbows close to your sides.
5. Palms facing away from you.
6. Feet shoulder-width apart with a slight bend in your knees.
7. Chest up, shoulders back, core braced.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Keeping your upper arms stationary, curl the barbell forward and up in a smooth arcing motion while exhaling.
2. Only your forearms should move — do not swing your body.
3. Continue upwards until the bar is at shoulder level with your biceps fully contracted.
4. Hold for a count of one while squeezing your biceps at the top.
5. Inhale as you slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner.
6. Fully extend your arms at the bottom without locking the elbows.
7. Repeat for the desired number of reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Swinging the body or using momentum to lift the weight
- Allowing the elbows to drift forward or flare out
- Not using a full range of motion
- Lowering the weight too quickly (missing the eccentric phase)
- Gripping the bar too tightly, causing forearm fatigue
- Leaning back excessively at the top of the movement
- Using too much weight and sacrificing form

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Straight Barbell or EZ Curl Bar
- Weight Plates
- Collars
- Optional: Wrist Wraps (for wrist support)
- Optional: Arm Blaster (to lock elbows in position)
- Optional: Lifting Gloves or Chalk (for grip)

sections.heading: Bar Setup
sections.content:
1. Select a straight barbell or EZ curl bar.
2. Load the appropriate weight evenly on both sides.
3. Secure the plates with collars.
4. Place the bar on a rack at hip height or pick it up from the floor using a deadlift motion.
5. Ensure enough clear space in front of and behind you.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet shoulder-width apart, stable base.
2. Grip: Underhand (supinated), shoulder-width apart.
3. Elbows: Pinned to the sides of your torso throughout.
4. Shoulders: Pulled back and depressed, not rounded forward.
5. Core: Braced to prevent swinging or swaying.
6. Knees: Slight bend to reduce lower back stress.
7. Head: Neutral position, eyes forward.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- EZ Bar Curl: Angled grip reduces wrist strain
- Dumbbell Bicep Curl: Unilateral, more range of motion
- Hammer Curl: Neutral grip targets brachialis
- Preacher Curl: Bench isolates biceps, eliminates momentum
- Cable Curl: Constant tension throughout the range of motion
- Concentration Curl: Seated isolation for peak contraction

sections.heading: Curl Variations
sections.content:
Wide-Grip Barbell Curl: Emphasises the short (inner) head of the biceps
Close-Grip Barbell Curl: Emphasises the long (outer) head of the biceps
21s: 7 lower half reps, 7 upper half reps, 7 full reps
Drag Curl: Bar drags up the body, elbows move behind you
Reverse Curl: Overhand grip for brachioradialis and forearm emphasis
Paused Curl: Pause at the midpoint for increased time under tension

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Wrist Pain: Use an EZ curl bar or switch to hammer curls
Elbow Issues: Reduce weight, avoid full lockout at the bottom
Lower Back Strain: Perform seated or use an arm blaster to prevent swinging
Grip Issues: Use lifting straps or switch to dumbbell curls
No Barbell: Use dumbbells, cables, or resistance bands
Learning Stage: Start with light weight, focus on slow controlled reps
